To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the member of construct in the UML can be used for the inheritance of properties and that a textual notation is needed to define data structures and contents in the course
of an analysis.

a) the member of construct can be used to define inheritance in UML static structures; b) the member of notation is a suitable means to define inheritance in the context of product data modelling; c) a data modelling language that is based on UML static structures and the member of notation can be applied to support the design of product data models for complex products; and d) a data modelling approach that is based on this language is suitable for the design of data models for the product data management system
a classification hierarchy is a data model that is based on the concept of generalisation and that it can be modelled in UML using the member of construct.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the modelling of data structures that represent classification hierarchies and their contents.
a data model that is capable of modelling classification hierarchies, and a textual notation that enables the definition of product data structures and contents in an iterative manner.
the development of a data modelling language that enables the definition of product data structures and the introduction of product data contents in a systematic way.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the UML class diagram is a suitable data modelling language for the representation of product data structures.
the proposed notation is an adequate means for the design and documentation of classification hierarchies in data models.
the member of construct is a very powerful construct that enables one not only to model the inheritance of data structures, but also the inheritance of data contents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the UML is a powerful modelling language for product data.

we have shown how the member of construct can be interpreted to enable the inheritance of product data in classification hierarchices, and how the UML can be enriched to support the modelling of product data.
a data model is an abstraction that represents data structures and data contents in the form of a classification hierarchy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the member of construct can be interpreted as an association that is used in the definition of a class and in the definition of its superclass.
the introduction of the member of notation in UML static structure diagrams enables one to model classification hierarchies that support inheritance of product properties.
data models should be capable of representing product hierarchies in a way that allows for the inheritance of product characteristics.
